QEVA
MapSandboxHistoryArchiveProtocol

GLOBAL CORPUS PIPELINE

Map the literature without copying the noise.

QEVA aims to index mathematics across history and current research. The ingestion layer gathers provenance; the logical layer decides what an extracted statement actually says and what supports it.

Non-negotiable separation

external work / book / paper
          ↓ provenance
  extracted candidate statement
          ↓ explicit assumptions + checking
      QEVA logical object

A paper node can be historically important and mathematically wrong. A theorem can be logically elementary but historically discovered late. QEVA therefore stores literature edges and logical edges as different types.

Initial source families

OpenAlex

Large connected scholarly graph of works, authors, venues, topics, and citations.

metadata backbone
Crossref

DOI metadata, references, licenses, funders, and update relations.

identifier + provenance reconciliation
arXiv

Modern open research metadata and source/full-text access under arXiv's reuse constraints.

frontier indexing; do not blindly redistribute
zbMATH Open

Math-specific bibliographic records, classifications, reviews, and citation matching.

mathematical literature structure
OEIS

Deep sequence corpus with formulas, references, transformations, and cross-links.

CC BY-SA source; preserve attribution/share-alike
Wikidata + historical libraries

Identity/date reconciliation plus public-domain primary sources and scans.

history layer; rights checked per source/item

“Scrape the internet” policy

  1. Prefer official APIs, dumps, OAI feeds, and bulk datasets over brittle HTML scraping.
  2. Respect robots directives, rate limits, API terms, copyright, database rights, and item-level licenses.
  3. Store metadata and provenance even when full text cannot legally be mirrored.
  4. Store full text only when public domain, openly licensed for that reuse, or otherwise permitted.
  5. Never bypass access controls or anti-bot systems.
  6. Hash imported snapshots when possible; record source URL, source identifier, retrieval time, and license.
  7. Keep machine extraction as candidate structure until reviewed or formally verified.

Scale architecture

source adapters
    ↓
raw immutable source records
    ↓
identity resolution / deduplication
    ↓
normalized works + citations + people + dates
    ↓
claim / definition / proof / problem extraction candidates
    ↓
logical qualification and human/formal review
    ↓
QEVA map + timeline + sandbox links

The current repo includes stdlib-only metadata adapters for OpenAlex, Crossref, and arXiv as reference implementations. They are intentionally small and replaceable.
